test_commands_and_results.detail: The committed contract is only byte-reproducible against POSTGRES. Generating under config.settings.test (SQLite, the documented fast local suite) yields sha256 03ee43ab5fb9d55e36e48c8b788ecb51a422d5601e3477a6bdfe9ae52679fd0a / 22155 lines, diverging in 20 places where an integer field's bounds move from int32 (2147483647) to int64 (9223372036854775807) with format: int64 added. Cause: Django derives IntegerField validators from connection.ops.integer_field_range(), and the SQLite backend returns 64-bit ranges for every integer field because SQLite does not enforce. Generation is deterministic within each environment (verified by a second run).
test_commands_and_results.why_it_matters: scripts/generate-api-types.sh writes DIRECTLY over backend/schema/openapi.v2.candidate.yaml and its DEFAULT DATABASE_URL is sqlite:///tmp/schema-gen.db, so running it with no env overrides silently rewrites the committed contract with the int64 variant. CI is safe today (.github/workflows/ci.yml and backend-governance.yml both set DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=config.settings.dev with a Postgres service), so this is a developer-workstation drift generator, not a live CI break.

new_findings.title: Nine foreign keys are permanently NOT VALID because three tables were created with the expand half of the expand/validate pattern and no validate half
new_findings.measured: 9 NOT VALID FKs on tenant_onboarding (2), tenant_staff_invitations (4) and tenant_change_requests (3), present in BOTH the fresh-from-empty schema and the Neon authoring branch. grep confirms no VALIDATE CONSTRAINT statement exists anywhere in backend/scripts/ for these three tables, while five other expand scripts do have a paired _validate.sql.
new_findings.reading: These are NEW tables, so there are no pre-existing rows to validate and the FK is enforced for every row that can exist — this is not a data-integrity hole today. The cost is that manage.py schema_manifest --verify can never return ok on any environment, so a real future violation would be indistinguishable from this permanent one, and the scripts' own comment ('validation of any pre-existing rows is deferred') describes work nobody scheduled.

new_findings.title: 72 backend tests have not run since task 9.4, and no gate noticed
new_findings.measured: Eight test modules patch apps.applications.document_views.AccessScopeService unconditionally. Task 9.4 rewired document_views onto the shared resolve_scoped_application seam and dropped that module-level import, so the patch target no longer exists and all eight ERROR at setup: 22 + 20 + 8 + 6 + 5 + 3 + 3 + 2 = 69 in unit, plus 3 more downstream, plus tests/property/test_application_endpoints.py's 13 and tests/property/test_interview_status_validation.py's 1 (interview_views._staff_can_access_application, the same shape). 86 tests total.
new_findings.reading: 9.4 hit this and fixed exactly one module — tests/unit/test_admin_export_hardening.py guards the patch with hasattr and documents why in a comment — and left the other eight. The correct shape is already in the tree, which is what makes this cheap. It matters because a test that errors at setup never runs, and 12.1 §15.1 is this spec's own precedent for why unrun tests make a gate unmeasurable: the 52-file selection every task from 12.1 to 12.5 measured contains none of these eight files, so the hole was invisible for five consecutive recordings.
new_findings.proposed_owner: the admin-query/scope lane that owns task 9.4

new_findings.title: The committed OpenAPI contract is only reproducible against Postgres, and the repo's own generator script defaults to SQLite
new_findings.measured: manage.py spectacular under config.settings.dev + Postgres reproduces backend/schema/openapi.v2.candidate.yaml byte-identically (35fe05d4…, 22135 lines). Under config.settings.test (SQLite) it produces 03ee43ab…, 22155 lines, with 20 integer-bound divergences (int32 -> int64 + format: int64). Django derives IntegerField validators from connection.ops.integer_field_range(); SQLite returns 64-bit ranges for every integer field.
new_findings.reading: scripts/generate-api-types.sh writes directly over the committed contract and defaults DATABASE_URL to sqlite:///tmp/schema-gen.db, so a developer running it unqualified rewrites the contract with the wrong variant and the generated client changes with it. CI is not affected: both workflows pin config.settings.dev against a Postgres service. The fix is one line in the script (or a vendor assertion in the schema guard).

new_findings.title: One rollback script is not inverse-additive, against R9.2
new_findings.measured: tests/property/test_rollback_safe_operations.py fails twice on 2026_07_16_02_canonical_assignment_backfill_rollback.sql: a statement matches no allowed inverse-additive form (DROP INDEX / DROP COLUMN / DROP TABLE / DROP SEQUENCE / DELETE FROM).
new_findings.reading: R9.2 requires every rollback statement to be inverse-additive. A backfill's rollback is the awkward case — undoing a data backfill is not a DROP — so this may be a genuine spec/instrument tension rather than a defect, and task 13.4 rehearses rollback. Reported, not resolved.

new_findings.title: R2.7's immutable evidence is not immutable: three instruments write into docs/v2-evidence/**
new_findings.measured: This gate rewrote 65 files across seven earlier task directories (11.5: 20, 11.4: 16, 11.3: 10, 11.2: 10, 11.1: 7, 2.2: 1, 0.4: 1) without this task writing into any of them. Three mechanisms: (1) apps/admissions/playwright.harness.config.ts:39 hard-codes the JSON reporter to ../../docs/v2-evidence/0.4/playwright-report.json, so EVERY harness run by ANY task overwrites task 0.4's Required_Evidence; (2) six required specs write screenshots into docs/v2-evidence/11.1-11.5/screenshots; (3) backend/tests/property/test_authority_matrix_generated.py:555 writes docs/v2-evidence/2.2/authority-conformance-summary.json, so running the backend suite overwrites task 2.2's Required_Evidence.
new_findings.reading: Not introduced by 13.1 — this is how those tasks PRODUCED their evidence, and each rewrite is a fresh capture of the same journey rather than an edit. But R2.7's guarantee does not hold for these five tasks' artifacts: they reflect whoever ran the gate last, not what that task measured on its date. 13.1 is the first task to trigger all three mechanisms in one run, which is why it surfaced here. Task 13.6 has to assert 'every required task evidenced' and is the bullet that most needs this to be true.
new_findings.not_restored: docs/v2-evidence/ is untracked in git and none of the five tasks recorded content hashes for these artifacts, so there is nothing to restore to. Current hashes of all 65 files are recorded instead.
new_findings.proposed_owner: the harness lane (task 0.4) owns mechanisms 1 and 2; task 2.2 owns mechanism 3

not_claimed: That the gate is clean. It is not: 179 backend tests, 1 frontend test, 15 lint errors, 2 browser tests, 1 bundle rule, 1 broken npm script and 4 schema/register items do not pass.

That any of the 146 never-catalogued backend items was investigated beyond attribution. They were measured, clustered and, for the 39-item remainder, listed individually with their messages. Nothing was fixed.
That the 39-item unattributed remainder has a cause. It has a name, a message and a location, and is explicitly labelled unattributed.

That the harness numbers are strong evidence on their own. 12.4 §12.2 established this machine is load-limited; two full-profile runs are recorded (218/2/0 then 216/3/1 on a byte-identical build) so the variance is visible, including where it moved the convenient way.

That design-system-defluff.spec.ts:664 was fixed or is a defect. Six measurements are recorded, no axe violation appears in any of them, it fails alone on a used stack and passes alone on a fresh one. Attributed to stack/box load and to a thin 30 s budget; not repaired.

That ocr-manual-fallback.spec.ts:146's earlier isolated failure was imaginary. It passed 4/4 project-runs here — evidence about this environment, not proof, and no cumulative cross-task total is asserted. The wizard lane still owns it.
That production was measured. Nothing touched production. The Neon reading is the authoring default branch, read-only, and 13.4/13.5 own the rehearsal and the canary.
That the register owner/removal-date gap was closed. It was re-measured unchanged and handed to 13.6.

That verify_migration.py was run. Task 3.1's schema_manifest tool supersedes it and reached three real databases; 0.5 recorded verify_migration.py as environment-blocked and nothing here changes that.
That the two-tenant golden/adversarial matrix, the mobile/zoom/a11y sweep, the migration rehearsal, the canary, or spec closure were performed. Those are 13.2-13.6.
That the 65 earlier-task evidence files the instruments rewrote were restored. They were not, and could not be — see GATE-13.1-07. Their current hashes are recorded instead.
rollback_decision: N/A — this task runs and records. No product source, schema, migration, register or deployment was changed. This task's own writes are docs/v2-evidence/13.1/** plus the tasks.md checkbox; one throwaway Postgres database (v2_fresh_13_1) created inside the isolated localtest container and then dropped; and the harness stack, torn down to 0 containers / 0 volumes. The one tracked file a measurement command rewrites (docs/launch-evidence/05-bundle/bundle-evidence.json) was restored and verified. Separately, the instruments themselves rewrote 65 files across seven earlier task evidence directories — finding GATE-13.1-07 — reported rather than restored, because nothing was recorded to restore to.
